title: Yes, transmission is dull. Read this article anyway.
gist: The author argues the IRA and IIJA neglected transmission — under 0.3% of energy spending and just $2.9 billion in direct funding against $1 trillion+ in energy provisions — which stranded much of the promised decarbonization and contributed to an exploding interconnection queue as US high-voltage line builds fell below 500 miles a year in 2021-2023. Future legislation should fund grid enablers via an investment tax credit, pursue permitting reform, and pay above-market rates for rights-of-way.

insights.claim: The IRA and IIJA largely neglected transmission enablers and focused on generation, which impeded deployment of the wind and solar generation they sought to build.
insights.so_what: Generation subsidies without wires create stranded or curtailed renewable capacity and grid bottlenecks.
insights.locator: Recent energy legislation has ignored it
insights.speaker: Atlantic Council

insights.claim: Princeton's REPEAT study found over 80 percent of the IRA's potential 2030 emissions reductions would be lost if transmission expansion stayed at one percent per year.
insights.so_what: Transmission is the binding constraint on US decarbonization outcomes.
insights.quote: of IRA’s potential emissions reductions by 2030 would be lost if transmission expansion remained at one percent per year
insights.locator: The IRA did not deliver its promised
insights.speaker: Atlantic Council

insights.claim: The IRA devoted less than 0.3 percent of energy spending to grid expansion — only $2.9 billion in direct transmission funding against energy provisions estimated at over $1 trillion for 2022-2031 — and had no investment tax credit for large transmission lines, reconductoring or dynamic line rating.
insights.so_what: Grid-enhancing technologies remain under-incentivized relative to generation — a potential policy catalyst if addressed.
insights.locator: The IRA and the IIJA were virtually silent
insights.speaker: Atlantic Council

insights.claim: The IRA over-prioritized new technologies with low or speculative social rates of return, priced externalities for generation but not for transmission.
insights.so_what: Critique from within the energy-policy community suggests future legislation may rebalance toward grid spending.
insights.locator: A new incentive program for building
insights.speaker: Atlantic Council

insights.claim: The US built fewer than 500 miles of high-voltage transmission per year in 2021-2023, down from nearly 4,000 miles in 2013 alone, while the interconnection queue exploded.
insights.so_what: Grid scarcity raises congestion costs, interconnection delays and power prices — tailwind for owners of existing transmission and grid-equipment suppliers.
insights.locator: With key grid technologies facing limited
insights.speaker: Atlantic Council

insights.claim: Transmission's key constraints are political and regulatory: HVDC developers must obtain permission from every jurisdiction lines cross, letting a single actor torpedo a project, and FERC Order 1920 on long-term planning only came in May 2024.
insights.so_what: Permitting reform is the key unlock for long-distance lines; absent it, build rates stay low.
insights.locator: Perhaps even more important than transmission’s
insights.speaker: Atlantic Council

insights.claim: The IIJA's $10.5 billion GRIP program was slow to disburse, with one investment announcement coming in October 2024, nearly three years after passage.
insights.so_what: Even funded grid programs face multi-year execution lags.
insights.quote: Transmission planning was overcooked; actual construction was underdone.
insights.locator: Where IRA and IIJA did fund transmission
insights.speaker: Atlantic Council

insights.claim: The One Big Beautiful Bill Act restricted clean energy incentives and did nothing for transmission, and the Trump administration has cancelled several transmission projects.
insights.so_what: Federal policy currently worsens the transmission bottleneck.
insights.locator: Recent energy legislation has ignored it
insights.speaker: Atlantic Council

insights.claim: A $3.5 billion Loans Program Office conditional guarantee for new lines issued in January 2025 was promptly paused by the Trump administration, which also cancelled three proposed National Interest Electric Transmission Corridors while launching a 'Corridors of Commerce' initiative of uncertain effectiveness.
insights.so_what: Mixed signals: watch whether Corridors of Commerce actually enables long-distance lines.
insights.locator: Indeed, the former Loans Program Office
insights.speaker: Atlantic Council

insights.claim: Policymakers should pass permitting reform and consider an investment tax credit for grid enablers covering reconductoring, dynamic line ratings and grid-enhancing technologies.
insights.so_what: A grid-enabler ITC would be a direct catalyst for reconductoring and GETs vendors.
insights.locator: In order to tackle the affordability crisis
insights.speaker: Atlantic Council

insights.claim: Federal legislation should fund direct payments to landowners and communities and pay above-market rates for rights-of-way to speed transmission, reflecting the social value of a more reliable, cleaner and often cheaper grid.
insights.so_what: Compensating hosts could reduce local opposition, the main blocker for new lines.

insights.speaker: Atlantic Council

insights.claim: Analysts were wrong-footed by Russia's invasion of Ukraine, the post-COVID demand snapback and AI's impact on electricity demand, but underprioritizing the grid was a costly technical mistake regardless.
insights.so_what: AI-driven load growth makes grid underinvestment more acute, reinforcing affordability pressure.
insights.locator: It’s admittedly far easier to second-guess
insights.speaker: Atlantic Council
